TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Economic Development Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
5:30 PM, October 13, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner K. Good at 5:33 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 The roll was called by the Clerk, and the following members were present: 
 
Present 
Commissioner Ken Good, Chair 
Commissioner Petra Gardella 
Commissioner Tammy Robinson 
Commissioner Anthony J. DelGrego 
Commissioner Howard K. Hill 
Commissioner Maggie Murolo 
 
Absent 
Commissioner Romeo Ibanez 
 
Also in attendance were Steve Fontana, Economic Development Director; Briana J. Belton-
Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk; and three members of the public, who attended 
virtually. 
 
Roll Call Summary: Present, Voting: 6; Present, Not Voting: 0; Absent: 1; Excused: 0. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
 
  1. Meeting Minutes for September 8th, 2026  
  Chairman K. Good requested a motion to adopt the minutes from Tuesday, 
September 8th, 2026, with the following corrections: 
 
Chairman K. Good requested that the attendance roll-call summary reflect seven 
voting members rather than eight.
Commissioner M. Maggie moved to approve the minutes with that correction, and 
Commissioner T. Robinson seconded the motion. 
 
Present 
Commissioner K. Good, Chair 
Commissioner T. Robinson 
Commissioner A.J. DelGrego 
Commissioner H.K. Hill 
Commissioner M. Murolo 
 
Absent 
Commissioner R. Ibanez 
 
Abstentions 
Commissioner P. Gardella 
 
The previous meeting minutes with corrections. 
 
The motion passed. 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 5, No 0, Abstentions 1, Absent 1. 
 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 
 
  1. Please limit your comments to three minutes.  
  Clerk B. Belton-Robinson read three written submissions sent directly to the 
Commission email: 
 
Diane Hoffman asked when the Commission incorporates trees and green 
infrastructure, including adequate tree pits, shade, stormwater management, and 
traffic-calming, into development planning and budgets. 
 
 
An Anonymous commenter, submitted through Sarah Clark, asked how business 
attraction could help lower the mill rate or offset its phase-in. 
 
Stocky Clark asked about financial due diligence and the capacity of nonprofit 
developers to complete large redevelopment projects. Mr. S. Clark also spoke, 
emphasizing predevelopment and construction cash-flow capacity.  
 
Commissioner P. Gardella commented that financial risks can arise with both 
nonprofit and for-profit developers. No further public comments were received. 
 
  
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 Chairman K. Good noted that the three written public submissions had been addressed 
during public comment. Clerk B. Belton-Robinson reported no additional correspondence. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No executive session was held. 
7. CHAIRMAN'S REPORTS 
  
 
 
  1. Business Community Update   
  Chairman K. Good reported activity at the newly opened Ross Dress for Less and 
Bagel Bagel at 2404 Whitney Avenue. He discussed opportunities for Hamden to 
attract businesses associated with the New Haven region’s growing quantum-
computing sector. He reported approximately 67 business registrations during 
September, including retail/food/personal care, real estate, 
professional/creative/technology, construction/property services, 
healthcare/education/social care, transportation/delivery, manufacturing/fabrication, 
and other businesses. He emphasized manufacturing as an opportunity to create jobs 
and expand the tax base. 
  2. EDC Alliances  
  Chairman K. Good described outreach to the University of New Haven, including a 
homecoming visit with Finance Commissioner Tom Fortuna, and continued 
engagement with Quinnipiac University through student-business mentoring and 
advisory discussions. Commissioners were encouraged to participate in future 
mentoring opportunities. 
  3. Finalizing 2027 Economic Development Meeting   
  Chairman Good presented the proposed 2027 meeting schedule, generally retaining 
meetings at 5:30 p.m. on the second Tuesday of each month with hybrid/in-person 
participation.  
 
After discussion and review of the dates, Commissioner T. Robinson moved to 
approve the calendar, and Commissioner P. Gardella seconded.  
 
Vote by Roll Call: 
 
Yes 
Commissioner Ken Good, Chairman 
Commissioner Petra Gardella 
Commissioner Tammy Robinson 
Commissioner Anthony J. DelGrego 
Commissioner Howard K. Hill 
Commissioner Maggie Murolo
No 
 
Absent 
Commissioner Romeo Ibanez 
 
The motion passed. 
 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 6, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 1. 
  
8. DIRECTOR'S REPORT 
  
 Director Stephen Fontana responded to the public comments and provided the following 
development and economic-development updates: 
 
 
• Trees and Green Infrastructure: The Town is working with the Tree Commission 
and Hamden Alliance for Trees on grant-supported planting in eligible southern 
Hamden neighborhoods. New development proposals may include landscaping 
plans reviewed through Planning and Zoning. 
• Business Attraction and Tax Base: Economic development and grand-list growth 
require multiple years. Director Fontana highlighted the potential for expansion by 
existing Sherman Avenue businesses and for multifamily development along major 
corridors, while noting financing, site availability, zoning, and infrastructure 
challenges. 
• High Meadows and Former Middle School: The Community Builders (TCB), 
selected through a prior competitive process, is advancing affordable-housing 
concepts for High Meadows. Further due diligence, public engagement, regulatory 
review, and financing remain ahead. No nonprofit developer was identified as 
currently managing redevelopment of the former Hamden Middle School property. 
• Town Center Master Plan: Consultant SLR is collecting survey and virtual-workshop 
input, with public engagement anticipated through October and preparation of draft 
recommendations thereafter. Director Fontana encouraged broader participation, 
including students, residents outside the town center and Quinnipiac stakeholders. 
Chairman Good noted 273 survey responses at the time of a prior project meeting. 
• Cooper House Square: Town approvals have been obtained; developers are 
working on financing and project phasing. 
• Hamden 2040: A public community conversation is being coordinated, with date 
and venue still to be determined. 
• 1666 Whitney Avenue (former Spring Glen Hardware): The property owners are 
developing a proposal and were encouraged to seek feedback from the Spring Glen 
Civic Association and nearby stakeholders. 
• Business Openings and Recruitment: Director Fontana discussed Ross Dress for 
Less and Bagel Bagel, and reported that Panda Express is expected to occupy part 
of the former Panera space at Hamden Plaza. Outreach to additional expanding 
businesses continues.
• Dixwell Reconnection Project: The Town plans to seek a Community Investment 
Fund grant for planning improvements connecting Dixwell Avenue with the Linear 
Trail, potentially including pedestrian/bicycle access, sidewalks, trees, parklets and 
public art. 
• 3360 Whitney Avenue: An easement request associated with the Linear Trail was 
before Planning and Zoning and could enable a small commercial development, 
subject to approvals. 
• Old Coach Highway: Town staff are reviewing development application materials; 
no public hearing date had been set at the time of the meeting. 
• Sewer Feasibility Study: A consultant is studying the technical and financial 
feasibility of extending sewer service north toward the Cheshire line. No 
implementation decision has been made. 
• Industrial Expansion Assistance Program: Director Fontana is preparing a 
submission to the Legislative Council to support industrial/commercial business 
expansion or relocation. 
 
Town Center Master Plan — Director S. Fontana’s project report and public participation 
resource; the survey will remain open through Saturday, October 31, 2026: 
https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/0f6a98a6ff694764a0bf687527e39584 
https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/9DM36MS 
 
The commission discussed housing density and affordability, project design, community 
input, and neighborhood concerns related to the Old Coach Highway proposal. 
9. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 Chairman K. Good reported that the planned Chamber-sponsored candidate meet-and-
greet had been canceled, and the town was exploring a smaller gathering. He also 
discussed damage to the town clock tower from a vehicle collision. Director S. Fontana 
stated that the Town Engineer was reviewing cost-effective repair or replacement options; 
no final decision was reported. Commissioner P. Gardella raised examples of housing-
development partnerships and second-home taxation for consideration. 
10. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 Chairman K. Good announced the Hamden Regional Chamber of Commerce Awards 
Dinner scheduled for November 12, 2026, at Cascades Fine Dining, and highlighted award 
recipients across business, civic, education, nonprofit, and environmental categories. A 
formal event announcement will be circulated to commissioners. 
11. ADJOURNMENT 
  
  Chairman K. Good reminded commissioners that the next month’s meeting (November) would 
be in person. 
 
Commissioner P. Gardella moved to adjourn; Commissioner H.K. Hill seconded.  
 
The motion passed unanimously.
The meeting adjourned at 6:50 PM.
